analysis:
The supplied units are base-side text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1248-1573); the change itself is a documentation-only patch in the head at lines 11-45, which adds a v0.10.13 candidate release-notes section. I examined the base excerpts and the patch excerpt. No source code, authorization logic, crypto, attestation or wire protocol is modified here, so no canonical threat-model control (TB-002, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041 and similar) is weakened by this diff.

Security-relevant claims in the new notes are descriptive and need verification against the actual code in other batches. First, the Gemma 4 loop guard (#2040) closes the thinking block and answers within an 8,192-token cap. It is stated to be disabled with logprobs and on pairs, and controlled by the DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING env var. Second, a user-requested stop now ends the leading Mac's start at once, including during download or load (#2042). Reviewers of the code PRs should check that stop handling cannot be triggered by an untrusted party, and that it leaves no stale authorization (T-053) or half-registered pair state.

The notes state that the registration fields, cluster runtime facts and MLX pins are unchanged, and that mlx.metallib is unchanged. That is an unverified claim, to be confirmed in the build and registration units, and it matters for A-017 and T-054 qualification evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remainder of the new section was not seen.

The older base-side changelog text covers items such as the waitlist, gpu-limit (TB-014/T-062), the sandbox installer (TB-013/T-061) and route keys. It is pre-existing and was not re-evaluated. The T-041 cache definition is not touched by this diff. No findings are raised, but deeper review of the code changes behind these notes is warranted because I could not verify them here.
